acceptance_criteria.criterion: src/cli/docs.ts compiles without errors and exports generateDocs()
src/cli/menu.ts compiles without errors and exports showMenu()
The menu displays all four options (Setup, GUI, Docs, Quit) with highlighted key shortcuts
The menu dispatches correctly to each action on keypress
Launch GUI loads config, starts the server, prints the URL, and attempts to open the browser
Generate Docs runs ctx generate if available, or displays installation instructions if not
The menu loops back after Setup and Docs actions complete
Launch GUI keeps the process running (does not return to menu)

summary: Implemented src/cli/docs.ts — exports generateDocs(). Uses spawnSync to check ctx availability (stdio:ignore), spawns ctx generate with inherited stdio for real-time output, resolves with success/failure message on process exit. Falls back to install instructions when ctx is not on PATH.

Implemented src/cli/menu.ts — exports showMenu(). Reads package.json version once (cached), runs a while(true) loop rendering clearScreen + printHeader + four printOption calls, dispatches on waitForKey(['s','g','d','q']). Implements private launchGui() (loads config, resolves staticDir, calls startServer, opens browser platform-specifically with detached+unref spawn, then awaits a never-resolving promise to keep the process alive). Implements pressAnyKeyToContinue() using a broad key set.
Build: tsc produced zero errors. All 539 existing tests pass (npm test).

comments.note: src/cli/menu.ts: pressAnyKeyToContinue() uses a hardcoded key list. A cleaner approach would be extending waitForKey() in terminal-ui.ts to accept an optional 'any' sentinel that uses a broader raw-mode read — but that is a terminal-ui enhancement outside this WP's scope.

src/cli/menu.ts: The never-resolving promise in launchGui() that keeps the process alive after startServer() is slightly unconventional. An explicit process.on('SIGINT') handler that calls stopServer() would give a cleaner shutdown path — noted as a future enhancement outside this WP's scope.

src/cli/docs.ts: isCtxAvailable() checks both result.error === undefined AND result.status !== null. The status !== null guard handles a rare edge case (SIGKILL), but could be simplified to just checking result.error for readability since a killed ctx --version is functionally equivalent to not found.

src/utils/paths.ts: Uses 'node:fs' in some imports (config.ts) but plain 'fs'/'path' in paths.ts itself (without the node: prefix). The project convention in newer files (setup.ts, index.ts, our new files) is to use 'node:' prefixed specifiers — paths.ts predates that convention and could be updated for consistency.

summary: QA validation complete for WP-003. Reviewed src/cli/docs.ts and src/cli/menu.ts against all 10 acceptance criteria. TypeScript compilation: zero errors (tsc --noEmit exit 0). Test suite: 539/539 passing, 0 failing. All acceptance criteria verified through static analysis and direct code inspection.
AC1-2 (compile + exports): Both files compile cleanly and export generateDocs() and showMenu() respectively.
AC3 (menu display): printOption() calls for S/G/D/Q all present with pc.bold(pc.yellow()) highlighting from terminal-ui.ts.
AC4 (dispatch): waitForKey(['s','g','d','q']) feeds into switch(key) routing to runSetup, launchGui, generateDocs, and return-quit.
AC5 (Launch GUI): launchGui() loads config via loadConfig(), calls startServer(), printSuccess(url), openBrowser(url). Error paths (config missing, server fail) return to menu correctly.
AC6 (Generate Docs): isCtxAvailable() uses spawnSync with stdio:ignore; runCtxGenerate() spawns with inherited stdio. Fallback prints install URL when ctx is not on PATH.
AC7 (loop back): Setup and Docs cases use break — correctly returns to while(true) loop head rather than exiting.
AC8 (keep process alive): launchGui() ends with await new Promise<never>(() => {}) after startServer() succeeds — the HTTP server event loop keeps Node.js running.
AC9 (clean quit): case 'q': return exits showMenu() cleanly.
AC10 (existing tests): 539/539 pass.

comments.note: Interactive TTY behaviour (raw-mode keypress dispatch, browser launch, server startup) is not covered by automated tests — this is inherent to the design and was flagged by the Developer in handoff notes. The logic paths are straightforward and low-risk; manual/integration testing is the appropriate vehicle.

src/cli/menu.ts launchGui(): if startServer() throws, the error is caught and the function returns to the menu. However, if startServer() resolves but then the server later crashes (post-start), there is no recovery path — the process would exit. This is acceptable behaviour for a CLI tool and is consistent with the existing server startup in src/index.ts.

src/cli/menu.ts pressAnyKeyToContinue(): the Ctrl+C key (\x03) is not in the accepted keys list, so pressing Ctrl+C during 'press any key' will exit the process (handled by waitForKey's \x03 guard) rather than continuing. This is actually correct behaviour — user can abort with Ctrl+C at any time — but worth noting it is intentional.

summary: Code review PASS for WP-003 (src/cli/docs.ts and src/cli/menu.ts). Both files are well-structured, clearly documented, and fully conformant with the WP-003 spec.

docs.ts: Clean separation of public API (generateDocs) from private helpers (isCtxAvailable, runCtxGenerate). Error handling is thorough: spawnSync ENOENT path, spawn 'error' event, and non-zero exit codes are all handled and reported to the user with actionable messages. The exit-code augmentation (code ?? 1) on the close event is a correct defensive guard for SIGKILL. JSDoc is complete and accurate.

menu.ts: showMenu() loop structure is idiomatic (while(true) + return-on-quit, break for looping actions). Version caching via module-level _version is correct and avoids repeated filesystem reads. launchGui() properly separates config-load failure (returns to menu) from server-start failure (returns to menu) from success (blocks forever). The await new Promise<never>() idiom is the right tool here since the server keeps the event loop alive — the comment explaining this is clear. openBrowser() correctly detaches and unrefs the child process. pressAnyKeyToContinue() comment and key list are clear.
All imports use 'node:' prefixed specifiers consistently within the new files. All public exports match the WP spec exactly. No dead code, no unused imports.
Minor observations recorded — all low-priority and pre-acknowledged by Developer/QA. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: src/cli/menu.ts launchGui(): the `return` on line 88 after `await launchGui()` in showMenu() is only reached when launchGui() returns early due to a config/server error. The comment on that line ('Reached only if launchGui() returns early (config error)') is accurate and important for future maintainers — it correctly distinguishes the two exit paths. No change needed; noting for documentation.

src/cli/menu.ts: launchGui() uses `config.serverPort ?? 4200` to compute the port locally (line 127) rather than relying on the defaults already baked into loadConfig(). Since loadConfig() already applies the 4200 default via DEFAULTS, config.serverPort will never be undefined after loadConfig() returns — the `?? 4200` is redundant but harmless. Could be simplified to just `config.serverPort` in a future cleanup.

src/cli/docs.ts: isCtxAvailable() returns `result.error === undefined && result.status !== null`. The double-guard is correct and the inline comment explains the SIGKILL edge case. Consistent with the cautious pattern used elsewhere in the codebase. Low-priority simplification candidate only.

src/utils/paths.ts (pre-existing): Uses plain 'fs'/'path' imports rather than 'node:fs'/'node:path' as used by all new CLI files. Not introduced by this WP, but worth addressing in a future housekeeping pass for consistency.
